summary: Wooden lighthouse on Île Brion, Magdalen Islands, first lit 1905, automated 1967; grounds and tower closed, reached by boat excursion.

lens.note: third-order dioptric apparatus installed September 1906 (1906 report, p. 51); the 1905 apparatus was catoptric

structures.note: 49 ft from base to lantern ventilator (1904 report); the register also gives 14.9 m. Original cast-iron lantern replaced by aluminium in 1969.

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard light. Grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Boat excursions in calm weather (LighthouseFriends). Ecological reserve since 1984 (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Boat of Spencer and William Turner shipwrecked on 4 December 1847; the Turners were later buried on the island (LighthouseFriends)
Steamer Indiana: her captain's course brought Bryon Island ahead; letter from Quebec, 10 September 1902
Department purchased 0.8 ha at the west end from William Dingwell (LighthouseFriends)
Erected under contract by E. F. Munro of Westville, N.S., contract price $5,497
Put in operation at the opening of navigation in 1905

Changed to a revolving red and white signal (1905 report). The 1904 plan was a group-revolving white light of 3 flashes; the 1906 report describes the temporary light as a group revolving light of three flashes. The sequence is not settled.
Third-order dioptric apparatus replaced the temporary apparatus in September 1906
Vessel Maskinonge stranded on Bryon Island on 5 August; the master was reprimanded at the Halifax inquiry, 11 September
Steamship printed as Frankmere (OCR reads Franlcmere; the page image reads Frankmere) towed off the southeast point and convoyed to Halifax, 8 to 29 August
Original cast-iron lantern replaced by an aluminium lantern (register)
Texaco subsidiary SAREP bought the island for oil exploration; no oil found (LighthouseFriends)
Station buildings other than the light tower demolished (LighthouseFriends)
Government purchased the island and established an ecological reserve of 650 ha (LighthouseFriends)
Declared a historic monument (LighthouseFriends). The station file records a recognised heritage immovable in 2006.

keepers.name: Procule Chevrier
keepers.note: Spelled 'Procule Chervier' by LighthouseFriends, which calls him the first keeper and gives head-keeper dates 1905 to 1918. Its narrative says 1905 to 1908. Marine lists show 'Chevrier, P' (1906, Byron Island row) and 'Procule Chevrier' (1908, 1909, Bryon Island row); on the page images each list gives appointment 23 June 1905 and salary $400. The 1918 end date is LighthouseFriends only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station file's built year 1905 is the year the light went into service. The 1904 report and LighthouseFriends describe a tower erected under contract in 1904 and lit at the 1905 opening of navigation.

The 1904 report gives 126 feet above high water (38.4 m). The station file's 40 m comes from the Canadian Coast Guard list, which was not read here. Both are recorded; the current list value should be checked.

The 1904 plan (group-revolving white, 3 flashes), the 1905 report (revolving red and white, temporary apparatus one red and two white flashes every two minutes) and the 1906 report (temporary light a group revolving light of three flashes) disagree. Stated in the story as unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-27. Image checks: the 1906, 1908 and 1909 keeper lists were read on the page images (scan 176, 192, 172): in each, the Byron/Bryon Island station sits on the same row as Chevrier (appointed 23 June 1905, salary $400); the 1906 entry is printed p. 167 and the 1908 entry p. 183, the 1909 entry p. 165. The 1904 page with the 'Bryon island' entry (scan 52) is printed p. 39. The 1906 Bryan Island paragraph (scan 58) is printed p. 51 of the Commissioner of Lights appendix. The 1918 steamer name is printed Frankmere (scan 106, printed p. 107), not Franlcmere as the OCR has it. The Maskinonge and Evans entries (scan 72, printed p. 73) are in running text in the OCR, not a column table; not image-checked. Corrections made in the story: the 1906 page is no longer 'printed page not confirmed'; the steamer name is corrected; the 1909 printed page is 165; the 'Plus de 700' register statement is a regional count (island region), not a count for this island; the opening's register citation now covers the tower height only; the 'stone and reefs' sentence, the general 'supplies came by sea' sentence and the 'reached only by boat' wording are removed; the 'letter to the Deputy Minister' is not claimed (the extract does not show the addressee); the Montcalm sentence now says what the report says (workmen and construction materials, not lighthouse supplies to Bird Rock and Brion Island specifically); the 19-mile range is stated without a unit (the report prints miles only). Open points: (1) Conflict: LighthouseFriends' narrative says Chervier kept the light 1905 to 1908; its head-keeper list says 1905 to 1918; the marine lists show him on the island in 1906, 1908 and 1909. The 1918 end date and all keepers after 1927 rest on LighthouseFriends alone. Marine reports after 1924 are not in the local corpus. (2) First signal unresolved (see resolved_conflicts). (3) Focal height 126 ft (38.4 m) in 1904 vs 40 m in the station file (CCG list not read). (4) Characteristic 'Fl W 3s' comes from LighthouseFriends prose; the CCG List of Lights entry was not read. (5) Montcalm: the first-trip year is not stated in the printed passage, so the story gives none; the OCR's 'Jidy 5' date is not used. (6) The Indiana letter's addressee is not shown in the extract. (7) LighthouseFriends' wreck count (at least fifty-six) is attributed, not checked. (8) Excluded on privacy grounds: LighthouseFriends' personal details about keepers' health, pension and families; keepers after about 1960 are listed here as the page prints them, not named in the story. (9) French translations are mine. (10) Cartier's 1534 naming is from LighthouseFriends; Cartier's log was not read.
